title: Canonical comparison and weakly contractible evaluation of derived morphism sheaves
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme with its small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and let $B$ be a commutative ring in $\mathrm{Type}(u+1)$. Use the actual set- and module-valued comparison inverse images $
u^*$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] and the derived local Hom/Isom presheaves and sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-morphism-presheaves]. The comparison on the slice over an etale object $V$ is the constructed sheaf inverse image of the postcomposition functor $(X_{\mathrm{et}}/V)	o(X_{\mathrm{proet}}/V)$. This functor is continuous, its module inverse image is exact, and the slice base-change morphism obtained by restricting the global adjunction unit and transposing under the slice adjunction is an invertible natural morphism. Derive this specified morphism to identify restriction of $
u^*$ with slice comparison. Pullback of actual local derived morphisms or isomorphisms, followed by pro-etale sheafification, is natural in $V$. Transpose this presheaf map first under sheafification and then under the comparison adjunction, defining the canonical sheaf maps $
u^*\mathcal H_{A,D}	o\mathcal H_{
u^*A,
u^*D}$ and $
u^*\mathcal I_{A,D}	o\mathcal I_{
u^*A,
u^*D}$.

For an affine object $U$ weakly contractible in the sense that every epimorphism of set sheaves is surjective on sections over $U$, the pro-etale sheafification units of the two actual local derived presheaves are bijections (the presheaves carry finite disjoint unions, including the empty union, to products). Define evaluation from the two pulled-back etale sheaves to actual derived Hom and Isom on the localized pro-etale site by composing the above sheaf maps with the unique inverse of these unit bijections. Define composition of pulled-back sections through the inverse-image product comparison, and the sections represented by actual etale-local maps through the sheafification and comparison units; identities are represented over the terminal etale object. For a ring map $B	o B'$, the scalar-restriction comparison $
u^*\operatorname{Res}	o\operatorname{Res}
u^*$ is the transpose of the restriction of the comparison unit; it is invertible and natural, and gives the specified comparison on derived categories. All maps here have the indicated canonical constructions, not freely chosen data.
